subject: Request: short launch safety valve — burst surcharge + escrow options
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha@brightlane.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlane.com
Date: 2026-10-12T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Request: short launch safety valve + invoice smoothing for launch

Hi Rachel,

Hope you’re well — we’re ramping into a public beta on Thursday and expect a short, high-volume spike for ~48–72 hours. Our finance team is worried about sudden overrun charges that could break our launch budget. Can Redwood offer a short-duration "safety valve" (temporary quota uplift + capped surcharge) and an invoice smoothing mechanism so the unexpected overrun doesn’t hit our weekly burn?

Quick details:
- Forecasted peak: ~12M tokens/day over a 48–72 hour window (attached deck)
- Current committed tier: 150k qps/month equivalent (we’re above baseline for the period)
- Procurement needs: a simple addendum or PO-friendly statement of work

We’re open to either: (A) a time-limited quota bump with standard overrun pricing, or (B) a short-term blended overrun rate + escrow deposit to cap exposure. Can you share what Redwood can do and any timelines for activation?

Thanks — Sam
Samantha Liu
Head of Platform, BrightLane
Attachment: BrightLane_Month1_forecast.xlsx

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha@brightlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short launch safety valve + invoice smoothing for launch

Sam — thanks for the context and the forecast. We can support a safety-valve approach; below are two practical options we can activate quickly. I’ve looped Ben (sales) for pricing and Laura (legal) for minimal addendum language, and Dev for activation lead time.

Option A — Fast uplift (operational):
- Temporary quota bump to X10 baseline for up to 72 hours
- Standard overrun pricing (per-token) applies; invoice as usual
- Activation: within 4–6 hours after we receive written PO/approval

Option B — Blended cap + escrow (finance-friendly):
- Temporary bump to X10 for up to 72 hours
- Blended overrun rate (e.g., 60% of list overrun) with a hard cap on billable surcharge for the window
- Client posts an escrow/deposit (one-time) covering the capped surcharge; remaining delta reconciled post-window and either refunded or invoiced in next cycle
- Activation: requires quick addendum signature (DocuSign) and escrow confirmation; typically 12–24 hours.

We prefer Option B for large launch spikes since it provides predictable cost exposure for BrightLane and lets us provision headroom without long-term commit changes. I attached a short term-sheet draft (proposed_safety_valve_term.pdf) for Laura’s review.

Next steps: if you prefer B, can procurement sign an addendum and wire the escrow? If you prefer A, send an approval email and Dev will queue the uplift.

— Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_safety_valve_term.pdf

Sam / Rachel — quick pricing breakdown so procurement can see the numbers to approve the escrow: (these are illustrative; final numbers in addendum)

Option A (fast uplift):
- Temporary X10 uplift for 72h; standard overrun = $0.12 / 1k tokens over committed baseline
- Worst-case exposure (based on your forecast): ~$110k

Option B (blended + cap):
- Temporary X10 uplift for 72h; blended surcharge = $0.07 / 1k tokens (40% discount to list overrun)
- If blended amount exceeds $50k cap, Redwood will only bill up to $50k (client escrow covers up to $50k)
- Reconciliation: single line on next invoice; unused escrow returned within 30 days

If finance wants the absolute $50k cap, we need escrow funded at that level and a signed addendum with the capped-surcharge language. Laura, can you confirm minimal legal text and whether the cap introduces any compliance flags on our side?

Thanks — Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Heads up on operational timing: we can gate a quota uplift in two ways — a soft route (config only) or a hard route (provision extra Dedicated headroom).

- Soft route: config change to routing/burst multiplier (activation < 6 hours). Works for most bursts but has softer latency guarantees.
- Hard route: spin up reserved headroom or hot-pool (activation ~8–12 hours depending on capacity). Better latency and KV cache warmup but requires more planning.

For Thursday 00:00 PT: if we receive DocuSign + escrow confirmation by 18:00 PT Wednesday, we can do the hard route; otherwise we can activate the soft route and then migrate.

Telemetry note: based on your attached forecast, we’ll need to prime KV caches for the main model to avoid cold-TTL tail latency; please confirm which model variant you’re using and expected request distribution (chat vs generate). See link: https://redwood-console.example.com/ops/telemetry/brightlane-launch

— Dev
